title: 해외 여행
intro: 해외 여행은 '가 본 나라·도시 묘사 → 여행 준비 과정 → 여행 중 문제·기억에 남는 일 → 과거와 현재 또는 국내 여행과 비교'로 출제됩니다. 작년 여름 가족(엄마, 아빠, 남동생 Junho)과 함께 간 일본 오사카(유니버설 스튜디오, 길거리 음식) 이야기 하나로 대부분의 질문을 해결하고, 비교 질문에는 고등학교 때의 첫 해외여행을 과거 이야기로 쓰세요.
strategy: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장(Okay, let me tell you about ~) → 언제·어디·누구와 → 거기서 한 일·먹은 음식 세부 → 느낌·좋았던 이유 → 마무리 문장(Yeah, that's ~)
도시는 오사카 하나로 고정: 유니버설 스튜디오, 도톤보리 길거리 음식(타코야키), 가족과 작년 여름. 묘사·경험·비교에 같은 장면을 재활용하세요.
문제 경험 질문은 '무슨 일 → 당황한 감정 → 해결 방법 → 배운 점' 4단계로 말하면 IH 이상 구조가 됩니다.
비교 질문은 고등학교 때 첫 해외여행(과거, 종이 지도·환전) vs 지금(앱·카드)으로 나누고 used to / these days 를 쓰세요.

expressions.en: Okay, let me tell you about my trip to Osaka.
expressions.ko: 좋아요, 제 오사카 여행에 대해 말씀드릴게요.
expressions.note: 해외 여행 질문의 시작 문장. 도시 이름만 바꿔 사용

expressions.en: I went to Japan with my family last summer.
The flight was only about an hour and a half.
expressions.ko: 비행시간이 한 시간 반 정도밖에 안 됐어요.

expressions.en: We tried a lot of street food.
expressions.ko: 길거리 음식을 정말 많이 먹어 봤어요.

expressions.en: I booked the flight and the hotel online.
I couldn't speak Japanese very well.
We got lost on the subway.
expressions.note: get lost: 길을 잃다 (과거 got lost)

expressions.en: I double-check my passport the night before.
expressions.ko: 전날 밤에 여권을 한 번 더 확인해요.

expressions.en: It was my first time traveling abroad.
Compared to traveling in Korea, it takes a lot more planning.
expressions.ko: 국내 여행에 비하면 훨씬 더 많은 계획이 필요해요.

expressions.en: Yeah, that's why Osaka is my favorite city so far.
expressions.ko: 네, 그래서 오사카가 지금까지 제일 좋아하는 도시예요.

expressions.en: I was so nervous that I couldn't think straight.
expressions.ko: 너무 긴장해서 제대로 생각을 못 했어요.

expressions.en: Looking back, it was actually a good lesson.

questions.en: You indicated in the survey that you like to travel abroad. Tell me about a country or city you have visited and really liked. What was it like, and what did you enjoy doing there?
questions.ko: 설문에서 해외 여행을 좋아한다고 하셨습니다. 가 본 나라나 도시 중 정말 좋았던 곳에 대해 말해 주세요. 어땠고, 거기서 무엇을 즐겼나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 언제·누구와·어디(작년 여름, 가족, 오사카) → 도시 분위기와 한 일(유니버설 스튜디오, 길거리 음식) → 좋았던 이유 → 마무리
도시 묘사는 '사람이 많고 활기차다, 깨끗하다, 음식이 싸고 맛있다'처럼 쉬운 형용사 3개로 충분해요.
'Seoul과 비슷하지만 ~는 다르다'는 비교 한 문장을 넣으면 IH 이상으로 들립니다.

answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you about my favorite city. It's Osaka in Japan. I went there with my family last summer. The flight from Seoul was only about an hour and a half. Osaka is a big and busy city, but it's very clean. We went to Universal Studios, and it was so much fun. We also tried a lot of street food, like takoyaki. Everything was cheap and delicious. I really want to go back. Yeah, that's my favorite city abroad.
answers.IH: Sure, I'd love to talk about a city I really liked. It's Osaka in Japan. I went there last summer with my family, my mom, my dad, and my younger brother Junho. The flight from Seoul was only about an hour and a half, so it was really easy. Osaka is a lot like Seoul because it's big and busy, but the people there seemed more relaxed and friendly. The highlight was Universal Studios. The lines were really long and it was super hot, but the rides were amazing, and Junho and I screamed the whole time. At night, we walked around Dotonbori, which is a famous street full of bright signs and food stalls. We tried takoyaki, okonomiyaki, and all kinds of street food. Honestly, the food alone was worth the trip. Yeah, that's why Osaka is my favorite city so far.
answers.AL: Oh, a city I've visited and really liked? Let me think. I'd definitely say Osaka in Japan. I went there last summer with my whole family, and it was our first overseas trip together in a long time. What I liked most about Osaka is that it has this really fun, lively energy. It's a huge city like Seoul, but people seemed a little more laid-back, and everyone we met was super kind to us, even though none of us speak Japanese very well. We spent one full day at Universal Studios. It was boiling hot and we waited in line for about an hour for each ride, but my brother Junho and I didn't care at all, because the rides were just that good. My parents mostly sat in the shade eating ice cream, which was honestly pretty cute. The best part, though, was the food. Every night, we went to Dotonbori, a street packed with neon signs and food stalls, and we just walked around trying everything we saw, like takoyaki and grilled skewers. I'm a big foodie, so that was basically heaven for me. Yeah, that's why Osaka is my favorite city so far, and I'm already saving money to go back.

questions.en: What do you usually do to prepare for a trip abroad? Tell me about all the steps you take, from booking the trip to packing your bags.
questions.ko: 해외 여행을 가기 전에 보통 무엇을 준비하나요? 예약부터 짐 싸기까지 거치는 모든 단계를 말해 주세요.
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 누구와 가는지 → 준비 순서(항공·호텔 예약 → 일정·맛집 검색 → 환전·유심 → 짐 싸기 → 여권 확인) → 준비할 때 느낌 → 마무리
First, Then, After that, Finally 로 단계를 연결하고 현재 시제로 습관을 말하세요.
오사카 여행 준비를 예시로 들면(엄마가 호텔 담당, 나는 맛집 담당) 구체적이고 자연스러워집니다.

answers.IM3: Sure, let me tell you how I prepare for a trip abroad. I usually travel with my family. First, we choose a place and a date. Then we book the flight and the hotel online. After that, I look for good restaurants and fun places on my phone. I also get some cash and a SIM card. Finally, I pack my bag. I always bring comfortable shoes and a charger. I check my passport two times. Yeah, that's how I get ready for a trip.
answers.IH: Okay, let me tell you about how I get ready for a trip abroad. I usually travel with my family, so we split up the work. First, my dad finds cheap flights, and my mom books the hotel. We try to book at least two months early, because prices go up really fast. Then my job is to make a list of places to go and things to eat. For example, before our trip to Osaka, I watched a lot of travel videos and found the best takoyaki places. After that, I exchange some money and buy a SIM card or a data plan online, so I can use maps there. A day or two before we leave, I pack my suitcase. I always bring comfortable shoes, a power adapter, and some medicine just in case. And of course, I double-check my passport the night before. So yeah, that's pretty much how I prepare for a trip abroad.
answers.AL: Oh, how I prepare for a trip abroad? Let me think. Well, I usually travel overseas with my family, and over the years we've kind of developed a system where everyone has a job. My dad is in charge of flights, because he's weirdly good at finding cheap tickets, and my mom takes care of the hotel. We usually book about two months in advance, since flight prices can basically double if you wait too long. My job is the fun part, which is planning what to do and, more importantly, what to eat. Before our trip to Osaka last summer, I spent hours watching travel vlogs and saving restaurants on my map app, and I even made a little schedule for each day. My brother Junho's only job is not to lose anything, which is honestly harder than it sounds for him. A week before the trip, I exchange some money and order a data plan online, so I can use maps and translation apps there. Then I pack a few days early, because I hate rushing at the last minute. I always bring comfortable sneakers, a power adapter, and some basic medicine. And the night before, I double-check everyone's passports, just to be safe. Yeah, that's basically how my family gets ready for a trip abroad.

questions.en: Have you ever had a problem or an unexpected situation while traveling abroad? Tell me about that experience in detail. What happened, and how did you deal with it?
questions.ko: 해외 여행 중에 문제가 생기거나 예상치 못한 상황을 겪은 적이 있나요? 그 경험을 자세히 말해 주세요. 무슨 일이 있었고 어떻게 해결했나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 언제·어디서(작년 여름 오사카) → 문제 상황(남동생과 지하철에서 길을 잃음) → 당황한 감정 → 해결 방법 → 배운 점과 마무리
과거 시제를 일관되게 쓰고, 'All of a sudden', 'Luckily', 'In the end' 로 이야기 흐름을 표시하세요.
AL은 감정 묘사(심장이 쿵쾅, 머리가 하얘짐)와 'Looking back' 반성 한 문장을 넣으세요.

answers.IM3: Oh, a problem while traveling? Let me think. Last summer, I went to Osaka with my family. One day, my brother Junho and I went shopping by ourselves. On the way back, we got lost on the subway. We took the wrong train, and my phone battery was almost dead. I was really scared. Luckily, a kind station worker helped us, and we found the right train. We got back to the hotel late. Yeah, that's a difficult moment I had abroad.
answers.IH: Sure, I'd love to talk about that. Last summer, I went to Osaka with my family, and something stressful happened. One afternoon, my brother Junho and I wanted to go shopping by ourselves, so we left our parents at the hotel. Everything was fine until we tried to come back. The subway system in Osaka is really complicated, and we got on the wrong train. All of a sudden, we were in a part of the city we didn't recognize at all. To make things worse, my phone battery was almost dead, so I couldn't use the map. I was really nervous, but I tried to stay calm for Junho. Luckily, we found a station worker, and even though I couldn't speak Japanese, I showed him our hotel name. He was so kind and wrote down the train and the stop for us. In the end, we got back safely, just an hour late. Yeah, that's the most stressful moment I've had abroad.
answers.AL: Oh, a problem while traveling abroad? Let me think. Yeah, I definitely have one. Last summer, my family and I went to Osaka, and on the third day, my brother Junho and I decided to go shopping on our own. I was feeling pretty confident because I had planned the whole trip on my phone. Shopping went great, but on the way back, we got on the wrong subway line. The Osaka subway is honestly like a maze, and before we knew it, we were somewhere totally unfamiliar. Then my phone battery died. I was so nervous that I couldn't think straight, and Junho kept asking me, 'Where are we?' which didn't help at all. So I took a deep breath and told myself to calm down. We walked up to a station worker, and since I don't speak Japanese, I used really simple English and showed him the hotel name on a receipt in my bag. He was incredibly patient. He wrote down which train to take, which stop to get off at, and he even walked us to the right platform. We made it back about an hour late, and my mom was pretty worried. Looking back, it was actually a good lesson. Now I always carry a portable charger. Yeah, that's a trip moment I'll never forget.

questions.en: How is the way you travel abroad now different from the first time you traveled overseas? Or, how does traveling abroad compare to traveling within Korea?
questions.ko: 지금 해외 여행하는 방식은 처음 해외여행을 했을 때와 어떻게 다른가요? 또는 해외 여행과 국내 여행은 어떻게 비교되나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 과거(고등학교 때 첫 해외여행: 종이 지도, 환전, 부모님 의존) → 현재(작년 오사카: 앱, 직접 계획) → 어느 쪽이 좋은지와 이유 → 마무리
국내 여행과 비교할 때는 '국내=친구들과 부산, 쉽고 편함 / 해외=가족과 오사카, 새롭고 계획이 더 필요'로 정리하세요.
used to, these days, compared to, a lot more ~ 같은 비교 표현을 2~3개 꼭 쓰세요.

answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you about how my trips abroad have changed. My first trip abroad was in high school. Back then, I didn't know anything, so my parents did everything for me. I was really nervous on the plane. Now it's different. Last summer, when we went to Osaka, I planned a lot of the trip. I used apps for maps and restaurants. Traveling is much easier now. Yeah, that's how my trips abroad have changed.
answers.IH: Sure, I'd love to talk about that. My first trip abroad was when I was in high school, and it was really different from how I travel now. Back then, I was really nervous because everything was new. I didn't even know how to check in at the airport, so I just followed my parents everywhere. We also had to exchange a lot of cash and carry a paper map. These days, things are much easier. When my family went to Osaka last summer, I planned most of the schedule by myself. I used a map app to find the subway, and I paid for almost everything with my card. I also used a translation app when I ordered food. I still love traveling with my family, but now I feel more like a helper, not just a kid. So yeah, that's pretty much how my trips abroad have changed.
answers.AL: Oh, how my trips abroad have changed? Let me think. Honestly, the difference between my first trip overseas and now is huge. My first trip abroad was back in high school, and I was so nervous that I barely slept the night before. I had no idea how airports worked, so I just followed my parents around like a little kid. My dad carried a thick envelope of cash, and we used a paper map that we kept getting wrong. These days, it's a totally different story. When my family went to Osaka last summer, I was actually the one leading the way. I planned most of our schedule, found the best restaurants through reviews, and figured out the subway on a map app. We paid for almost everything with our cards, and whenever I couldn't read a menu, I just pointed my phone's camera at it to translate it. Compared to the past, traveling is way more convenient now. But to be honest, I kind of miss that feeling from my first trip, when everything felt mysterious and exciting. Now I know what to expect, so it's a little less of an adventure. Still, I love that I can take care of my family a bit. Yeah, that's how the way I travel abroad has changed.

pronunciation.tip: 두 번째 음절 '브로-'에 강세. 첫 a는 약하게 '어'로 흘려요.
첫 음절 '패'에 강세. 끝 t는 살짝 끊듯이 약하게.
'수트케이스'. suit의 t는 거의 들리지 않게 멈추듯 발음해요.
미국식은 '스케줄', s 다음에 k 소리를 분명히 내세요.
